chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdill, from Ibn Sinan, from 'Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man wears a single garment up to his chest, he may pray in it.

He said: And I read in a letter of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), asking him about the fennec fox [skin], whether one may pray in it, so he wrote: There is no problem with it.
And I wrote asking him about the skins of rabbits, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: It is disliked.
And I wrote asking him about a garment lined with silk, whether one may pray in it, so he wrote: There is no problem with it.
ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on praying in different animal skins and silk-lined garments according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details specific jurisprudential rulings on the permissibility of praying in various garments, emphasizing that a single garment reaching the chest is sufficient for prayer. It distinguishes between materials, noting that while fennec fox skin and silk-lined garments are permissible, rabbit skin is considered disliked (makruh). These rulings reflect the practical application of purity and modesty principles in Shia fiqh, derived from the Imams' responses to specific material inquiries.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ahmad Bin Ibdeel, form Ibn Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Simt, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The man, when he wears a trouser with one cloth up to his chest, he can pray Salāt in it’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I read in a letter of Muhammad Bin Ibrahim to Abu Al-Hassanasws, asking himasws about the fennec fox, can one pray Salāt in it?’ So heasws wrote: ‘There is no problem with it’. And I wrote asking him about the skins of the rabbits, so heasws wrote: ‘It is disliked’. And I wrote asking himasws about the cloth lined with silk, can one pray Salāt in it?’ So heasws wrote: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Ahmad ibn ’Abddeyl from ibn Sinan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jundab from Sufyan ibn al-Simt who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a man covers himself with a loincloth up to his two breast he can perform Salah (prayer) with it.

He (the narrator) has said that he read in the letter of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in which he had asked about fennec if it is permissible to perform Salah (prayer) with it. He (the Imam) had written, ‘It is not an offense to perform Salah (prayer) with it.’
He had written asking about the skins of foxes and he (the Imam) had written, ‘It is undesirable.’
He had written asking about lining of silk (not the one from silkworm) if performing Salah (prayer) with it is permissible. He (the Imam) had written, ‘It is permissible.’”
